21: An ultra-fast cross-platform multiple screenshots module in pure python using ctypes.
22: 
23: - **Python 3.10+**, PEP8 compliant, no dependency, thread-safe;
24: - very basic, it will grab one screenshot by monitor or a screenshot of all monitors and save it to a PNG file;
25: - but you can use PIL and benefit from all its formats (or add yours directly);
26: - integrate well with Numpy and OpenCV;
27: - it could be easily embedded into games and other software which require fast and platform optimized methods to grab screenshots (like AI, Computer Vision);
28: - get the [source code on GitHub](https://github.com/BoboTiG/python-mss);
29: - learn with a [bunch of examples](https://python-mss.readthedocs.io/stable/examples.html);
30: - you can [report a bug](https://github.com/BoboTiG/python-mss/issues);
31: - need some help? Use the tag *python-mss* on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/python-mss);
32: - and there is a [complete, and beautiful, documentation](https://python-mss.readthedocs.io) :)
33: - **MSS** stands for Multiple ScreenShots;
34: 
35: 
36: ## Installation
37: 
38: You can install it with pip:
39: 
40: ```shell
41: python -m pip install -U --user mss
42: ```
43: 
44: Or you can install it with Conda:
45: 
46: ```shell
47: conda install -c conda-forge python-mss
48: ```
49:

class ScreenShot:
    """Screenshot object.

    .. note::
        A better name would have been *Image*, but to prevent collisions
        with PIL.Image, it has been decided to use *ScreenShot*.
    """

    __slots__ = {"__bgra", "__pixels", "__rgb", "_raw", "pos", "size"}

    def __init__(self, data: Buffer, monitor: Monitor, /, *, size: Size | None = None) -> None:
        self.__bgra: memoryview | None = None
        self.__pixels: Pixels | None = None
        self.__rgb: memoryview | None = None

        #: NamedTuple of the screenshot coordinates.
        self.pos: Pos = Pos(monitor["left"], monitor["top"])

        #: NamedTuple of the screenshot size.
        self.size: Size = Size(monitor["width"], monitor["height"]) if size is None else size

        # Buffer of the raw BGRA pixels, retrieved by the
        # platform-specific implementations.  This is kept read-write
        # if it was originally so, in order for _merge to work.
        # However, it should be made read-only before returning to the
        # user (via bgra), so that the cached values for __pixels and
        # __rgb aren't potentially inconsistent if the user changes
        # data.
        self._raw: memoryview = memoryview(data)
        assert self._raw.nbytes == self.size.width * self.size.height * 4, (  # noqa: S101
            "Data size does not match screenshot dimensions."

def to_png(data: bytes, size: tuple[int, int], /, *, level: int = 6, output: Path | str | None = None) -> bytes | None:
    """Dump data to a PNG file.  If `output` is `None`, create no file but return
    the whole PNG data.

    :param bytes data: RGBRGB...RGB data.
    :param tuple size: The (width, height) pair.
    :param int level: PNG compression level (see :py:func:`zlib.compress()` for details).
    :param str output: Output file name.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0.0

    .. versionchanged:: 3.2.0
       Added the ``level`` keyword argument to control the PNG compression level.
    """
    pack = struct.pack
    crc32 = zlib.crc32

    width, height = size
    line = width * 3
    png_filter = pack(">B", 0)
    scanlines = b"".join([png_filter + data[y * line : y * line + line] for y in range(height)])

    magic = pack(">8B", 137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10)

    # Header: size, marker, data, CRC32
    ihdr = [b"", b"IHDR", b"", b""]
    ihdr[2] = pack(">2I5B", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    ihdr[3] = pack(">I", crc32(b"".join(ihdr[1:3])) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    ihdr[0] = pack(">I", len(ihdr[2]))

    # Data: size, marker, data, CRC32
    idat = [b"", b"IDAT", zlib.compress(scanlines, level), b""]
    idat[3] = pack(">I", crc32(b"".join(idat[1:3])) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    idat[0] = pack(">I", len(idat[2]))

    # Footer: size, marker, None, CRC32
    iend = [b"", b"IEND", b"", b""]
    iend[3] = pack(">I", crc32(iend[1]) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    iend[0] = pack(">I", len(iend[2]))

66	def depends_on(subobject: Any, superobject: Any) -> None:
67	    """Make sure that superobject is not GC'd before subobject.
68	
69	    In XCB, a structure often is allocated with additional trailing
70	    data following it, with special accessors to get pointers to that
71	    extra data.
72	
73	    In ctypes, if you access a structure field, a pointer value, etc.,
74	    then the outer object won't be garbage collected until after the
75	    inner object.  (This uses the ctypes _b_base_ mechanism.)
76	
77	    However, when using the XCB accessor functions, you don't get that
78	    guarantee automatically.  Once all references to the outer
79	    structure have dropped, then we will free the memory for it (the
80	    response structures XCB returns have to be freed by us), including
81	    the trailing data.  If there are live references to the trailing
82	    data, then those will become invalid.
83	
84	    To prevent this, we use depends_on to make sure that the
85	    outer structure is not released before all the references to the
86	    inner objects have been cleared.
87	    """
88	    # The implementation is quite simple.  We create a finalizer on the inner object, with a callback that references
89	    # the outer object.  That ensures that there are live references to the outer object until the references to the
90	    # inner object have been gc'd.  We can't just create a ref, though; it seems that their callbacks will only run if
91	    # the ref itself is still referenced.  We need the extra machinery that finalize provides, which uses an internal
92	    # registry to keep the refs alive.
93	    finalize(subobject, id, superobject)

1: """GDI-based backend for MSS on Microsoft Windows.
2: 
3: Uses user32/gdi32 APIs to capture the desktop and enumerate monitors.
4: This implementation uses CreateDIBSection for direct memory access to pixel data.
5: """
6: 
7: from __future__ import annotations
8: 
9: import ctypes
10: import sys
11: from ctypes import POINTER, WINFUNCTYPE, Structure, WinError, _Pointer
12: from ctypes.wintypes import (
13:     BOOL,
14:     BYTE,
15:     DWORD,
16:     HANDLE,
17:     HBITMAP,
18:     HDC,

24:     LPARAM,
25:     LPRECT,
26:     LPVOID,
27:     RECT,
28:     UINT,
29:     WORD,
30: )

32: 
33: from mss.base import MSSImplementation
34: from mss.exception import ScreenShotError
35: 
36: if TYPE_CHECKING:
37:     from collections.abc import Callable
38:     from typing import Any
39: 
40:     from mss.models import CFunctionsErrChecked, Monitor, Monitors
41: 
42: __all__ = ()
43: 
44: 
45: LPCRECT = POINTER(RECT)  # Actually a const pointer, but ctypes has no const.
46: CAPTUREBLT = 0x40000000
47: DIB_RGB_COLORS = 0
48: SRCCOPY = 0x00CC0020
49: CCHDEVICENAME = 32
50: MONITORINFOF_PRIMARY = 0x01
51: EDD_GET_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NAME = 0x00000001
52:

54: class BITMAPINFOHEADER(Structure):
55:     """Information about the dimensions and color format of a DIB."""
56: 
57:     _fields_ = (
58:         ("biSize", DWORD),
59:         ("biWidth", LONG),
60:         ("biHeight", LONG),
61:         ("biPlanes", WORD),
62:         ("biBitCount", WORD),
63:         ("biCompression", DWORD),
64:         ("biSizeImage", DWORD),
65:         ("biXPelsPerMeter", LONG),
66:         ("biYPelsPerMeter", LONG),
67:         ("biClrUsed", DWORD),
68:         ("biClrImportant", DWORD),
69:     )
70: 
71: 
72: class BITMAPINFO(Structure):
73:     """Structure that defines the dimensions and color information for a DIB."""
74: 
75:     # The bmiColors entry is variable length, but it's unused the way we do things.  We declare it to be four bytes,
76:     # which is how it's declared in C.
77:     _fields_ = (("bmiHeader", BITMAPINFOHEADER), ("bmiColors", BYTE * 4))

80: class MONITORINFOEXW(Structure):
81:     """Extended monitor information structure.
82:     https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-monitorinfoexw
83:     """
84: 
85:     _fields_ = (
86:         ("cbSize", DWORD),
87:         ("rcMonitor", RECT),
88:         ("rcWork", RECT),
89:         ("dwFlags", DWORD),
90:         ("szDevice", WORD * CCHDEVICENAME),
91:     )
92: 
93: 
94: class DISPLAY_DEVICEW(Structure):  # noqa: N801
95:     """Display device information structure.
96:     https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/ns-wingdi-display_devicew
97:     """
98: 
99:     _fields_ = (
100:         ("cb", DWORD),
101:         ("DeviceName", WORD * 32),
102:         ("DeviceString", WORD * 128),
103:         ("StateFlags", DWORD),
104:         ("DeviceID", WORD * 128),
105:         ("DeviceKey", WORD * 128),
106:     )

109: MONITORNUMPROC = WINFUNCTYPE(BOOL, HMONITOR, HDC, POINTER(RECT), LPARAM)

112: def _check_result(result: int | _Pointer, func: Callable, arguments: tuple) -> tuple:
113:     """Raise if ``result`` is 0/NULL for functions that do not document GetLastError."""
114:     if not result:
115:         details = {
116:             "func": func.__name__,
117:             "args": arguments,
118:             "error_msg": "The function returned a failure value.",
119:         }
120:         msg = f"Windows graphics function returned failure: {func.__name__}"
121:         raise ScreenShotError(msg, details=details)
122:     return arguments
123: 
124: 
125: def _check_result_with_last_error(result: int | _Pointer, func: Callable, arguments: tuple) -> tuple:
126:     """Raise if ``result`` is 0/NULL for functions that document GetLastError."""
127:     if not result:
128:         error_code = ctypes.get_last_error()
129:         details = {
130:             "func": func.__name__,
131:             "args": arguments,
132:             "error_code": error_code,
133:         }
134:         if error_code == 0:
135:             # Do not use WinError(0) here: its message is "The operation completed successfully", which makes the
136:             # failure look like a success.
137:             details["error_msg"] = (
138:                 "The function returned a failure value, but no Windows last-error code was available."
139:             )
140:             msg = f"Windows graphics function returned failure but no last-error code was available: {func.__name__}"
141:             raise ScreenShotError(msg, details=details)
142:         # Notably, the errno that is in winerror may not be relevant.  Use the winerror and strerror attributes instead.
143:         winerror = WinError(error_code)
144:         details["error_msg"] = winerror.strerror
145:         msg = f"Windows graphics function failed: {func.__name__}: {winerror.strerror}"
146:         raise ScreenShotError(msg, details=details) from winerror
147:     return arguments

152: # Available attr: gdi32, user32.
153: #
154: # Note: keep it sorted by cfunction.
155: CFUNCTIONS: CFunctionsErrChecked = {
156:     # Syntax: cfunction: (attr, argtypes, restype, errcheck)
157:     "BitBlt": ("gdi32", [HDC, INT, INT, INT, INT, HDC, INT, INT, DWORD], BOOL, _check_result_with_last_error),
158:     "CreateCompatibleDC": ("gdi32", [HDC], HDC, _check_result),
159:     # CreateDIBSection: ppvBits (4th param) receives a pointer to the DIB pixel data.
160:     # hSection is NULL and offset is 0 to have the system allocate the memory.
161:     "CreateDIBSection": (
162:         "gdi32",
163:         [HDC, POINTER(BITMAPINFO), UINT, POINTER(LPVOID), HANDLE, DWORD],
164:         HBITMAP,
165:         _check_result_with_last_error,
166:     ),
167:     "DeleteDC": ("gdi32", [HDC], BOOL, _check_result),
168:     "DeleteObject": ("gdi32", [HGDIOBJ], BOOL, _check_result),
169:     "EnumDisplayDevicesW": ("user32", [POINTER(WORD), DWORD, POINTER(DISPLAY_DEVICEW), DWORD], BOOL, None),
170:     "EnumDisplayMonitors": ("user32", [HDC, LPCRECT, MONITORNUMPROC, LPARAM], BOOL, _check_result),
171:     # GdiFlush flushes the calling thread's current batch of GDI operations.
172:     # This ensures DIB memory is fully updated before reading.
173:     "GdiFlush": ("gdi32", [], BOOL, None),
174:     # While GetSystemMetrics will return 0 if the parameter is invalid, it will also sometimes return 0 if the
175:     # parameter is valid but the value is actually 0 (e.g., SM_CLEANBOOT on a normal boot).  Thus, we do not attach an
176:     # errcheck function here.
177:     "GetSystemMetrics": ("user32", [INT], INT, None),
178:     "GetMonitorInfoW": ("user32", [HMONITOR, POINTER(MONITORINFOEXW)], BOOL, _check_result),
179:     "GetWindowDC": ("user32", [HWND], HDC, _check_result),
180:     "ReleaseDC": ("user32", [HWND, HDC], INT, _check_result),
181:     # SelectObject returns NULL on error the way we call it.  If it's called to select a region, it returns HGDI_ERROR
182:     # on error.
183:     "SelectObject": ("gdi32", [HDC, HGDIOBJ], HGDIOBJ, _check_result),
184: }

187: class MSSImplGdi(MSSImplementation):
188:     """Multiple ScreenShots implementation for Microsoft Windows (GDI backend).
189: 
190:     This implementation uses CreateDIBSection for direct memory access to pixel data,
191:     which eliminates the need for GetDIBits. The DIB pixel data is written directly
192:     to system-managed memory that we can read from.
193: 
194:     This backend is selected by ``backend="default"`` and has no Windows-specific
195:     constructor parameters.
196: 
197:     .. seealso::
198: 
199:         :py:class:`mss.MSS`
200:             Lists constructor parameters.
201:     """
202: 
203:     __slots__ = {
204:         "_bmi",
205:         "_dib",
206:         "_dib_array",
207:         "_dib_bits",
208:         "_region_width_height",
209:         "gdi32",
210:         "user32",
211:     }
212: 
213:     def __init__(self) -> None:
214:         super().__init__()
215: 
216:         # user32 and gdi32 should not be changed after initialization.
217:         self.user32 = ctypes.WinDLL("user32", use_last_error=True)
218:         self.gdi32 = ctypes.WinDLL("gdi32", use_last_error=True)
219:         self._set_cfunctions()
220:         self._set_dpi_awareness()
221: 
222:         # Available instance-specific variables
223:         self._region_width_height: tuple[int, int] | None = None
224:         self._dib: HBITMAP | None = None
225:         self._dib_bits: LPVOID = LPVOID()  # Pointer to DIB pixel data
226:         self._dib_array: ctypes.Array[ctypes.c_char] | None = None  # Cached array view of DIB memory
227: 
228:         bmi = BITMAPINFO()
229:         bmi.bmiHeader.biSize = ctypes.sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER)
230:         # biWidth and biHeight are set in grab().
231:         bmi.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1  # Always 1
232:         bmi.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32  # 32-bit RGBX
233:         bmi.bmiHeader.biCompression = 0  # 0 = BI_RGB (no compression)
234:         bmi.bmiHeader.biSizeImage = 0  # Windows infers the size
235:         bmi.bmiHeader.biXPelsPerMeter = 0  # Unspecified
236:         bmi.bmiHeader.biYPelsPerMeter = 0  # Unspecified
237:         bmi.bmiHeader.biClrUsed = 0
238:         bmi.bmiHeader.biClrImportant = 0
239:         self._bmi = bmi
240: 
241:     def close(self) -> None:
242:         if self._dib:
243:             self.gdi32.DeleteObject(self._dib)
244:             self._dib = None
245: 
246:     def _set_cfunctions(self) -> None:
247:         """Set all ctypes functions and attach them to attributes."""
248:         cfactory = self._cfactory
249:         attrs = {
250:             "gdi32": self.gdi32,
251:             "user32": self.user32,
252:         }
253:         for func, (attr, argtypes, restype, errcheck) in CFUNCTIONS.items():
254:             cfactory(attrs[attr], func, argtypes, restype, errcheck)
255: 
256:     def _set_dpi_awareness(self) -> None:
257:         """Set DPI awareness to capture full screen on Hi-DPI monitors."""
258:         version = sys.getwindowsversion()[:2]
259:         if version >= (6, 3):
260:             # Windows 8.1+
261:             # Here 2 = PROCESS_PER_MONITOR_DPI_AWARE, which means:
262:             #     per monitor DPI aware. This app checks for the DPI when it is
263:             #     created and adjusts the scale factor whenever the DPI changes.
264:             #     These applications are not automatically scaled by the system.
265:             ctypes.windll.shcore.SetProcessDpiAwareness(2)
266:         elif (6, 0) <= version < (6, 3):
267:             # Windows Vista, 7, 8, and Server 2012
268:             self.user32.SetProcessDPIAware()
269: 
270:     def monitors(self) -> Monitors:
271:         int_ = int
272:         user32 = self.user32
273:         get_system_metrics = user32.GetSystemMetrics
274: 
275:         monitors = []
276: 
277:         # All monitors
278:         monitors.append(
279:             {
280:                 "left": int_(get_system_metrics(76)),  # SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN
281:                 "top": int_(get_system_metrics(77)),  # SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN
282:                 "width": int_(get_system_metrics(78)),  # SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN

344:     def grab(self, monitor: Monitor, /) -> bytearray:
345:         """Retrieve all pixels from a monitor using CreateDIBSection.
346: 
347:         Device contexts (srcdc / memdc) are acquired and released within each
348:         call.  This avoids holding GDI resources across threads and allows
349:         ``MSS()`` construction to succeed even when ``GetWindowDC(0)`` would
350:         fail (locked screen, UAC, RDP).  See issue #509.
351: 
352:         Note on biHeight: A bottom-up DIB is specified by setting the height to a
353:         positive number, while a top-down DIB is specified by setting the height
354:         to a negative number. We use negative height for top-down orientation.
355:         https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/ns-wingdi-bitmapinfoheader
356:         https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-createdibsection
357:         """
358:         gdi = self.gdi32
359:         srcdc = self.user32.GetWindowDC(0)
360:         try:
361:             memdc = gdi.CreateCompatibleDC(srcdc)
362:             try:
363:                 width, height = monitor["width"], monitor["height"]
364: 
365:                 if self._region_width_height != (width, height):
366:                     self._region_width_height = (width, height)
367:                     self._bmi.bmiHeader.biWidth = width
368:                     self._bmi.bmiHeader.biHeight = -height  # Negative for top-down DIB
369: 
370:                     if self._dib:
371:                         gdi.DeleteObject(self._dib)
372:                         self._dib = None
373: 
374:                     # CreateDIBSection creates the DIB and returns a pointer to the pixel data
375:                     self._dib_bits = LPVOID()
376:                     self._dib = gdi.CreateDIBSection(
377:                         memdc,
378:                         self._bmi,
379:                         DIB_RGB_COLORS,
380:                         ctypes.byref(self._dib_bits),
381:                         None,  # hSection = NULL (system allocates memory)
382:                         0,  # offset = 0
383:                     )
384: 
385:                     # Create a ctypes array type that maps directly to the DIB memory.
386:                     # This avoids the overhead of ctypes.string_at() creating an intermediate bytes object.
387:                     size = width * height * 4
388:                     array_type = ctypes.c_char * size
389:                     self._dib_array = ctypes.cast(self._dib_bits, POINTER(array_type)).contents
390: 
391:                 # Select the cached DIB into the per-call memdc so BitBlt writes into it.
392:                 gdi.SelectObject(memdc, self._dib)
393: 
394:                 # BitBlt copies screen content directly into the DIB's memory
395:                 gdi.BitBlt(memdc, 0, 0, width, height, srcdc, monitor["left"], monitor["top"], SRCCOPY | CAPTUREBLT)
396: 
397:                 # Flush GDI operations to ensure DIB memory is fully updated before reading.
398:                 gdi.GdiFlush()
399: 
400:                 # Read directly from DIB memory via the cached array view
401:                 assert self._dib_array is not None  # noqa: S101  for type checker
402:                 return bytearray(self._dib_array)
403:             finally:
404:                 gdi.DeleteDC(memdc)
405:         finally:
406:             self.user32.ReleaseDC(0, srcdc)

2: 
3: This is the fastest Linux backend available, and will work in most common
4: cases. However, it will not work over remote X connections, such as over ssh.
5: 
6: This implementation prefers shared-memory captures for performance and will
7: fall back to XGetImage when the MIT-SHM extension is unavailable or fails at
8: runtime. The fallback reason is exposed via ``performance_status`` to aid
9: debugging.
10: 
11: .. versionadded:: 10.2.0
12: """

14: from __future__ import annotations

16: import enum
17: import os
18: from mmap import PROT_READ, mmap  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

24: from mss.linux.xcbhelpers import LIB, XProtoError

26: if TYPE_CHECKING:
27:     from mss.models import Monitor
28: 
29: __all__ = ()

31: 
32: class ShmStatus(enum.Enum):
33:     """Availability of the MIT-SHM extension for this backend."""
34: 
35:     UNKNOWN = enum.auto()  # Constructor says SHM *should* work, but we haven't seen a real GetImage succeed yet.
36:     AVAILABLE = enum.auto()  # We've successfully used XShmGetImage at least once.
37:     UNAVAILABLE = enum.auto()  # We know SHM GetImage is unusable; always use XGetImage.
38:

40: class MSSImplXShmGetImage(MSSImplXCBBase):
41:     """XCB backend using XShmGetImage with an automatic XGetImage fallback.
42: 
43:     .. seealso::
44:         :py:class:`mss.linux.base.MSSImplXCBBase`
45:             Lists constructor parameters.
46:     """
47: 
48:     def __init__(self, *, display: str | bytes | None = None, with_cursor: bool = False) -> None:
49:         super().__init__(display=display, with_cursor=with_cursor)
50: 
51:         # These are the objects we need to clean up when we shut down.  They are created in _setup_shm.
52:         self._memfd: int | None = None
53:         self._buf: mmap | None = None
54:         self._shmseg: xcb.ShmSeg | None = None
55: 
56:         # Rather than trying to track the shm_status, we may be able to raise an exception in __init__ if XShmGetImage
57:         # isn't available.  The factory in linux/__init__.py could then catch that and switch to XGetImage.
58:         # The conditions under which the attach will succeed but the xcb_shm_get_image will fail are extremely
59:         # rare, and I haven't yet found any that also will work with xcb_get_image.
60:         #: Whether we can use the MIT-SHM extensions for this connection.
61:         #: This will not be ``AVAILABLE`` until at least one capture has succeeded.
62:         #: It may be set to ``UNAVAILABLE`` sooner.
63:         self.shm_status: ShmStatus = self._setup_shm()
64: 
65:     def _shm_report_issue(self, msg: str, *args: Any) -> None:
66:         """Debugging hook for troubleshooting MIT-SHM issues.
67: 
68:         This will be called whenever MIT-SHM is disabled.  The optional
69:         arguments are not well-defined; exceptions are common.
70:         """
71:         full_msg = msg
72:         if args:
73:             full_msg += " | " + ", ".join(str(arg) for arg in args)
74:         self.performance_status.append(full_msg)
75: 
76:     def _setup_shm(self) -> ShmStatus:  # noqa: PLR0911
77:         assert self.conn is not None  # noqa: S101
78: 
79:         try:
80:             shm_ext_data = xcb.get_extension_data(self.conn, LIB.shm_id)
81:             if not shm_ext_data.present:
82:                 self._shm_report_issue("MIT-SHM extension not present")
83:                 return ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE
84: 
85:             # We use the FD-based version of ShmGetImage, so we require the extension to be at least 1.2.
86:             shm_version_data = xcb.shm_query_version(self.conn)
87:             shm_version = (shm_version_data.major_version, shm_version_data.minor_version)
88:             if shm_version < (1, 2):
89:                 self._shm_report_issue("MIT-SHM version too old", shm_version)
90:                 return ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE
91: 
92:             # We allocate something large enough for the root, so we don't have to reallocate each time the window is
93:             # resized.
94:             self._bufsize = self.pref_screen.width_in_pixels * self.pref_screen.height_in_pixels * 4
95: 
96:             if not hasattr(os, "memfd_create"):
97:                 self._shm_report_issue("os.memfd_create not available")
98:                 return ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE
99:             try:
100:                 self._memfd = os.memfd_create("mss-shm-buf", flags=os.MFD_CLOEXEC)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
101:             except OSError as e:
102:                 return self._shm_unavailable("memfd_create failed", e)
103:             os.ftruncate(self._memfd, self._bufsize)
104: 
105:             try:
106:                 self._buf = mmap(self._memfd, self._bufsize, prot=PROT_READ)  # type: ignore[call-arg]
107:             except OSError as e:
108:                 return self._shm_unavailable("mmap failed", e)
109:             self._shmseg = xcb.ShmSeg(xcb.generate_id(self.conn).value)
110:             try:
111:                 # This will normally be what raises an exception if you're on a remote connection.
112:                 # XCB will close _memfd, on success or on failure.
113:                 try:
114:                     xcb.shm_attach_fd(self.conn, self._shmseg, self._memfd, read_only=False)
115:                 finally:
116:                     self._memfd = None
117:             except xcb.XError as e:
118:                 return self._shm_unavailable("Cannot attach MIT-SHM segment", e)
119:         except Exception:
120:             self._shutdown_shm()
121:             raise
122: 
123:         return ShmStatus.UNKNOWN
124: 
125:     def _shm_unavailable(self, msg: str, exc: Exception) -> ShmStatus:
126:         self._shm_report_issue(msg, exc)
127:         self._shutdown_shm()
128:         return ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE

131:         self._shutdown_shm()
132:         super().close()

134:     def _shutdown_shm(self) -> None:
135:         # It would be nice to also try to tell the server to detach the shmseg, but we might be in an error path
136:         # and don't know if that's possible.  It's not like we'll leak a lot of them on the same connection anyway.
137:         # This can be called in the path of partial initialization.
138:         if self._buf is not None:
139:             self._buf.close()
140:             self._buf = None
141:         if self._memfd is not None:
142:             os.close(self._memfd)

145:     def _grab_xshmgetimage(self, monitor: Monitor) -> bytearray:
146:         if self.conn is None:
147:             msg = "Cannot take screenshot while the connection is closed"
148:             raise ScreenShotError(msg)
149:         assert self._buf is not None  # noqa: S101
150:         assert self._shmseg is not None  # noqa: S101
151: 
152:         required_size = monitor["width"] * monitor["height"] * 4
153:         if required_size > self._bufsize:
154:             # This is temporary.  The permanent fix will depend on how
155:             # issue https://github.com/BoboTiG/python-mss/issues/432 is resolved.
156:             msg = (
157:                 "Requested capture size exceeds the allocated buffer. If you have resized the screen, "
158:                 "please recreate your MSS object."
159:             )
160:             raise ScreenShotError(msg)
161: 
162:         img_reply = xcb.shm_get_image(
163:             self.conn,
164:             self.drawable,
165:             monitor["left"],
166:             monitor["top"],
167:             monitor["width"],
168:             monitor["height"],
169:             ALL_PLANES,
170:             xcb.ImageFormat.ZPixmap,
171:             self._shmseg,
172:             0,
173:         )
174: 
175:         if img_reply.depth != self.drawable_depth or img_reply.visual != self.drawable_visual_id:
176:             # This should never happen; a window can't change its visual.
177:             msg = (
178:                 "Server returned an image with a depth or visual different than it initially reported: "
179:                 f"expected {self.drawable_depth},{hex(self.drawable_visual_id.value)}, "
180:                 f"got {img_reply.depth},{hex(img_reply.visual.value)}"
181:             )
182:             raise ScreenShotError(msg)

184:         # Snapshot the buffer into new bytearray.
185:         new_size = monitor["width"] * monitor["height"] * 4
186:         # Slicing the memoryview creates a new memoryview that points to the relevant subregion.  Making this and then
187:         # copying it into a fresh bytearray is much faster than slicing the mmap object.  Make sure we don't hold an
188:         # open memoryview if an exception happens, since that will prevent us from closing self._buf during the stack
189:         # unwind.
190:         with memoryview(self._buf) as img_mv:
191:             return bytearray(img_mv[:new_size])

193:     def grab(self, monitor: Monitor) -> bytearray:
194:         """Retrieve all pixels from a monitor. Pixels have to be RGBX."""
195:         if self.shm_status == ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE:
196:             return super()._grab_xgetimage(monitor)

198:         # The usual path is just the next few lines.
199:         try:
200:             rv = self._grab_xshmgetimage(monitor)
201:             if self.shm_status != ShmStatus.AVAILABLE:
202:                 self.shm_status = ShmStatus.AVAILABLE
203:                 self.performance_status.append("MIT-SHM is working correctly.")
204:         except XProtoError as e:
205:             if self.shm_status != ShmStatus.UNKNOWN:
206:                 # We know XShmGetImage works, because it worked earlier.  Reraise the error.

209:             # Should we engage the fallback path?  In almost all cases, if XShmGetImage failed at this stage (after
210:             # all our testing in __init__), XGetImage will also fail.  This could mean that the user sent an
211:             # out-of-bounds request.  In more exotic situations, some rare X servers disallow screen capture

214:             try:

224:             # Using XShmGetImage failed, and using XGetImage worked.  Use XGetImage in the future.
225:             self._shm_report_issue("MIT-SHM GetImage failed", e)
226:             self.shm_status = ShmStatus.UNAVAILABLE
227:             self._shutdown_shm()

232: # The atom cache needs to be per-connection. Rather than keying on a (connection, name) tuple, we use a two-level

260: def intern_atom(
261:     xcb_conn: Connection | _Pointer[Connection],
262:     name: str,
263:     *,
264:     only_if_exists: bool = False,
265: ) -> Atom | None:
266:     if name in _PREDEFINED_ATOMS:
267:         return _PREDEFINED_ATOMS[name]
268: 
269:     if isinstance(xcb_conn, _Pointer):
270:         # Dereference the pointer before using the cache.
271:         xcb_conn = xcb_conn.contents
272:     cache_key = addressof(xcb_conn)
273:     if cache_key not in _ATOM_CACHE:
274:         # This can happen if the connection was closed and its cache cleared, but some code still has a reference to
275:         # the connection object.  We could re-create the cache entry, but it's safer to just fail instead of silently
276:         # allowing lookups to succeed when they shouldn't.
277:         msg = "Connection to X server is closed"
278:         raise XError(msg)
279:     if name in _ATOM_CACHE[cache_key]:
280:         return _ATOM_CACHE[cache_key][name]
281: 
282:     # Atom names are required to be Latin-1, per the X protocol spec, although anything that's not in the XPCS (a
283:     # subset of ASCII) is vendor-defined.
284:     name_encoded = name.encode("latin_1", errors="strict")
285:     cookie = LIB.xcb.xcb_intern_atom(xcb_conn, 1 if only_if_exists else 0, len(name_encoded), name_encoded)
286:     atom_as_xid = cookie.reply(xcb_conn).atom
287:     if atom_as_xid.value == 0:
288:         if not only_if_exists:

290:             msg = f"X server failed to intern atom '{name}'"
291:             raise XError(msg)
292:         # We don't do negative caching, since any app might intern the atom at any time.
293:         return None

368:     prefetch_extension_data(conn_p, LIB.shm_id)
369:     prefetch_extension_data(conn_p, LIB.xfixes_id)
370: 
371:     _ATOM_CACHE[addressof(conn_p.contents)] = {}

373:     return conn_p.contents, pref_screen_num.value

34: # A quick refresher on why this module spends so much effort on object lifetimes, and how the pieces fit together:
35: #
36: # 1. Shape of XCB replies.
37: #    Each reply that comes back from libxcb is one contiguous allocation that looks like:
38: #       [fixed-size header][optional padding][embedded arrays/lists]
39: #    The protocol spec describes where those trailing lists live, but callers are not expected to compute offsets by
40: #    hand.  Instead, XCB exposes helper functions such as `xcb_setup_pixmap_formats` (returns pointer + length for a
41: #    fixed-size array) or iterator factories for nested variable-length data.  As long as the original reply is still
42: #    allocated, all of the derived pointers remain valid.
43: #
44: # 2. What ctypes does (and does not) track automatically.
45: #    When user code reads `my_struct.foo`, ctypes returns another ctypes object that still refers to memory owned by
46: #    `my_struct`; it does not copy the value.  To keep that relationship alive, ctypes silently sets `_b_base_` on the
47: #    derived object so the garbage collector knows that `my_struct` must stay around.  This mechanism only works when
48: #    ctypes itself materializes the derived object.
49: #
50: # 3. Why XCB accessors break that safety net.
51: #    The XCB helpers we need - `xcb_setup_pixmap_formats`, `xcb_randr_get_screen_resources_crtcs`, etc. - return raw C
52: #    pointers.  ctypes happily converts them to Python objects, but because the conversion went through a plain C
53: #    call, `_b_base_` never gets filled in.  The GC no longer realizes that the derived array depends on the reply, so
54: #    once every direct reference to the reply drops, libc is free to `free()` the allocation.  Any later access
55: #    through the derived pointer becomes undefined behaviour.
56: #
57: # 4. How this module keeps everything safe.
58: #    After every call into an XCB accessor we immediately call `depends_on(child, parent)`.  That helper installs a
59: #    finalizer on `child` whose only job is to keep a reference to `parent`.  No extra work is performed; the callback
60: #    holding the reference is enough to keep the reply alive until the child objects disappear.  Separately, when we
61: #    first receive the reply, we register another finalizer that hands the pointer back to libc once *all* dependants
62: #    have been collected.  As a result, higher-level code can treat these helper functions just like the XCB C API:
63: #    grab the array you need, keep it as long as you like, and trust that it stays valid.
64: 
65: 
66: def depends_on(subobject: Any, superobject: Any) -> None:
67:     """Make sure that superobject is not GC'd before subobject.
68: 
69:     In XCB, a structure often is allocated with additional trailing
70:     data following it, with special accessors to get pointers to that
71:     extra data.
72: 
73:     In ctypes, if you access a structure field, a pointer value, etc.,
74:     then the outer object won't be garbage collected until after the
75:     inner object.  (This uses the ctypes _b_base_ mechanism.)
76: 
77:     However, when using the XCB accessor functions, you don't get that
78:     guarantee automatically.  Once all references to the outer
79:     structure have dropped, then we will free the memory for it (the
80:     response structures XCB returns have to be freed by us), including
81:     the trailing data.  If there are live references to the trailing
82:     data, then those will become invalid.
83: 
84:     To prevent this, we use depends_on to make sure that the
85:     outer structure is not released before all the references to the
86:     inner objects have been cleared.
87:     """
88:     # The implementation is quite simple.  We create a finalizer on the inner object, with a callback that references
89:     # the outer object.  That ensures that there are live references to the outer object until the references to the
90:     # inner object have been gc'd.  We can't just create a ref, though; it seems that their callbacks will only run if
91:     # the ref itself is still referenced.  We need the extra machinery that finalize provides, which uses an internal
92:     # registry to keep the refs alive.
93:     finalize(subobject, id, superobject)

139: #### Request / response handling
140: #
141: # The following recaps a lot of what's in the xcb-requests(3) man page, with a few notes about what we're doing in
142: # this library.
143: #
144: # In XCB, when you send a request to the server, the function returns immediately.  You don't get back the server's
145: # reply; you get back a "cookie".  (This just holds the sequence number of the request.)  Later, you can use that
146: # cookie to get the reply or error back.
147: #
148: # This lets you fire off requests in rapid succession, and then afterwards check the results.  It also lets you do
149: # other work (like process a screenshot) while a request is in flight (like getting the next screenshot).  This is
150: # asynchronous processing, and is great for performance.
151: #
152: # In this program, we currently don't try to do anything asynchronously, although the design doesn't preclude it.
153: # (You'd add a synchronous=False flag to the entrypoint wrappers below, and not call .check / .reply, but rather just
154: # return the cookie.)
155: #
156: # XCB has two types of requests.  Void requests don't return anything from the server.  These are things like "create
157: # a window".  The typed requests do request information from the server.  These are things like "get a window's size".
158: #
159: # Void requests all return the same type of cookie.  The only thing you can do with the cookie is check to see if you
160: # got an error.
161: #
162: # Typed requests return a call-specific cookie with the same structure.  They are call-specific so they can be
163: # type-checked.  (This is the case in both XCB C and in this library.)
164: #
165: # XCB has a concept of "checked" or "unchecked" request functions.  By default, void requests are unchecked.  For an
166: # unchecked function, XCB doesn't do anything to let you know that the request completed successfully.  If there's an
167: # error, then you need to handle it in your main loop, as a regular event.  We always use the checked versions
168: # instead, so that we can raise an exception at the right place in the code.
169: #
170: # Similarly, typed requests default to checked, but have unchecked versions.  That's just to align their error
171: # handling with the unchecked void functions; you always need to do something with the cookie so you can get the
172: # response.
173: #
174: # As mentioned, we always use the checked requests; that's unlikely to change, since error-checking with unchecked
175: # requests requires control of the event loop.
176: #
177: # Below are wrappers that set up the request / response functions in ctypes, and define the cookie types to do error
178: # handling.

192:     def __init__(self, xcb_conn: Connection, xcb_err: GenericErrorStructure) -> None:
193:         if isinstance(xcb_err, _Pointer):

197:         details = {
198:             "error_code": xcb_err.error_code,
199:             "sequence": xcb_err.sequence,
200:             "resource_id": xcb_err.resource_id,
201:             "minor_code": xcb_err.minor_code,
202:             "major_code": xcb_err.major_code,
203:             "full_sequence": xcb_err.full_sequence,

206:         # xcb-errors is a library to get descriptive error strings, instead of reporting the raw codes.  This is not
207:         # installed by default on most systems, but is quite helpful for developers.  We use it if it exists, but
208:         # don't force the matter.  We can't delay this lookup until we format the error message, since the XCB
209:         # connection may be gone by then.
210:         if LIB.errors:
211:             # We don't try to reuse the error context, since it's per-connection, and probably will only be used once.
212:             ctx = POINTER(XcbErrorsContext)()
213:             ctx_new_setup = LIB.errors.xcb_errors_context_new(xcb_conn, ctx)
214:             if ctx_new_setup == 0:
215:                 try:
216:                     # Some of these may return NULL, but some are guaranteed.
217:                     ext_name = POINTER(c_char_p)()
218:                     error_name = LIB.errors.xcb_errors_get_name_for_error(ctx, xcb_err.error_code, ext_name)
219:                     details["error"] = error_name.decode("ascii", errors="replace")
220:                     if ext_name:
221:                         ext_name_str = ext_name.contents.value
222:                         # I'm pretty sure it'll always be populated if ext_name is set, but...
223:                         if ext_name_str is not None:
224:                             details["extension"] = ext_name_str.decode("ascii", errors="replace")
225:                     major_name = LIB.errors.xcb_errors_get_name_for_major_code(ctx, xcb_err.major_code)
226:                     details["major_name"] = major_name.decode("ascii", errors="replace")
227:                     minor_name = LIB.errors.xcb_errors_get_name_for_minor_code(
228:                         ctx, xcb_err.major_code, xcb_err.minor_code
229:                     )
230:                     if minor_name:
231:                         details["minor_name"] = minor_name.decode("ascii", errors="replace")
232:                 finally:
233:                     LIB.errors.xcb_errors_context_free(ctx)

235:         super().__init__("X11 Protocol Error", details=details)

238:         msg = super().__str__()
239:         details = self.details
240:         error_desc = f"{details['error_code']} ({details['error']})" if "error" in details else details["error_code"]
241:         major_desc = (
242:             f"{details['major_code']} ({details['major_name']})" if "major_name" in details else details["major_code"]
243:         )
244:         minor_desc = (

251:             + (f"\n  Minor opcode of failed request:  {minor_desc}" if details["minor_code"] != 0 else "")

258: class CookieBase(Structure):
259:     """Generic XCB cookie.
260: 
261:     XCB does not export this as a base type.  However, all XCB cookies
262:     have the same structure, so this encompasses the common structure
263:     in Python.
264:     """
265: 
266:     # It's possible to add a finalizer that will raise an exception if a cookie is garbage collected without being
267:     # disposed of (through discard, check, or reply).  If we ever start using asynchronous requests, then that would
268:     # be good to add.  But for now, we can trust the wrapper functions to manage the cookies correctly, without the
269:     # extra overhead of these finalizers.
270: 
271:     _fields_ = (("sequence", c_uint),)
272: 
273:     def discard(self, xcb_conn: Connection) -> None:
274:         """Free memory associated with this request, and ignore errors."""
275:         LIB.xcb.xcb_discard_reply(xcb_conn, self.sequence)

278: class VoidCookie(CookieBase):
279:     """XCB cookie for requests with no responses.

281:     This corresponds to xcb_void_cookie_t.
282:     """

284:     def check(self, xcb_conn: Connection) -> None:
285:         """Verify that the function completed successfully.
286: 
287:         This will raise an exception if there is an error.
288:         """
289:         err_p = LIB.xcb.xcb_request_check(xcb_conn, self)
290:         if not err_p:
291:             return
292:         err = copy(err_p.contents)
293:         LIB.c.free(err_p)
294:         raise XProtoError(xcb_conn, err)

297: class ReplyCookieBase(CookieBase):
298:     _xcb_reply_func = None
299: 
300:     def reply(self, xcb_conn: Connection) -> Structure:
301:         """Wait for and return the server's response.
302: 
303:         The response will be freed (with libc's free) when it, and its
304:         descendents, are no longer referenced.
305: 
306:         If the server indicates an error, an exception is raised
307:         instead.
308:         """
309:         err_p = POINTER(GenericErrorStructure)()
310:         assert self._xcb_reply_func is not None  # noqa: S101
311:         reply_p = self._xcb_reply_func(xcb_conn, self, err_p)
312:         if err_p:
313:             # I think this is always NULL, but we can free it.
314:             if reply_p:
315:                 LIB.c.free(reply_p)
316:             # Copying the error structure is cheap, and makes memory management easier.
317:             err_copy = copy(err_p.contents)
318:             LIB.c.free(err_p)
319:             raise XProtoError(xcb_conn, err_copy)
320:         assert reply_p  # noqa: S101
321: 
322:         # It's not known, at this point, how long the reply structure actually is: there may be trailing data that
323:         # needs to be processed and then freed.  We have to set a finalizer on the reply, so it can be freed when
324:         # Python is done with it.  The whole dependency tree, though, leads back to this object and its finalizer.
325:         # Importantly, reply_void_p does not carry a reference (direct or indirect) to reply_p; that would prevent
326:         # it from ever being freed.
327:         reply_void_p = c_void_p(addressof(reply_p.contents))
328:         finalizer = finalize(reply_p, LIB.c.free, reply_void_p)
329:         finalizer.atexit = False
330:         return reply_p.contents

339:     This arranges for the ctypes function to take the given argtypes.
340:     The ctypes function will then return an XcbTypedCookie (rather,

342:     XCB xcb_blahblah_reply function to check for errors and return the

354:     reply_func.argtypes = [POINTER(Connection), cookie_type, POINTER(POINTER(GenericErrorStructure))]

559: #### Trailing data accessors
560: #
561: # In X11, many replies have the header (the *Reply structures defined above), plus some variable-length data after it.
562: # For instance, XcbScreen includes a list of XcbDepth structures.
563: #
564: # These mostly follow two patterns.
565: #
566: # For objects with a constant size, we get a pointer and length (count), cast to an array, and return the array
567: # contents.  (This doesn't involve copying any data.)
568: #
569: # For objects with a variable size, we use the XCB-provided iterator protocol to iterate over them, and return a
570: # Python list.  (This also doesn't copy any data, but does construct a list.)  To continue the example of how
571: # XcbScreen includes a list of XcbDepth structures: a full XcbDepth is variable-length because it has a variable
572: # number of visuals attached to it.
573: #
574: # These lists with variable element sizes follow a standard pattern:
575: #
576: # * There is an iterator class (such as XcbScreenIterator), based on the type you're iterating over.  This defines a
577: #   data pointer to point to the current object, and a rem counter indicating the remaining number of objects.
578: # * There is a function to advance the iterator (such as xcb_screen_next), based on the type of iterator being
579: #   advanced.
580: # * There is an initializer function (such as xcb_setup_roots_iterator) that takes the container (XcbSetup), and
581: #   returns an iterator (XcbScreenIterator) pointing to the first object in the list.  (This iterator is returned by
582: #   value, so Python can free it normally.)
583: #
584: # The returned structures are actually part of the allocation of the parent pointer: the POINTER(XcbScreen) objects
585: # point to objects that were allocated along with the XcbSetup that we got them from.  That means that it is very
586: # important that the XcbSetup not be freed until the pointers that point into it are freed.
587: 
588: 
589: ### Iteration utility primitives
590: 
591: 
592: def list_from_xcb(iterator_factory: Callable, next_func: Callable, parent: Structure | _Pointer) -> list:
593:     iterator = iterator_factory(parent)
594:     items: list = []
595:     while iterator.rem != 0:
596:         current = iterator.data.contents
597:         # Keep the parent reply alive until consumers drop this entry.
598:         depends_on(current, parent)
599:         items.append(current)
600:         next_func(iterator)
601:     return items
602: 
603: 
604: def array_from_xcb(pointer_func: Callable, length_func: Callable, parent: Structure | _Pointer) -> Array:
605:     pointer = pointer_func(parent)
606:     length = length_func(parent)
607:     if length and not pointer:
608:         msg = "XCB returned a NULL pointer for non-zero data length"
609:         raise ScreenShotError(msg)
610:     array_ptr = cast(pointer, POINTER(pointer._type_ * length))
611:     array = array_ptr.contents
612:     depends_on(array, parent)
613:     return array

28: class MSSImplXCBBase(MSSImplementation):
29:     """Base class for XCB-based screenshot implementations.

31:     Provides common XCB initialization and monitor detection logic that can be
32:     shared across different XCB screenshot methods (``XGetImage``,
33:     ``XShmGetImage``, ``XComposite``, etc.).

35:     :param display: Optional keyword argument.
36:         Specifies an X11 display string to connect to.  The default is

38:     :type display: str | bytes | None

45:     def __init__(self, *, display: str | bytes | None = None, with_cursor: bool = False) -> None:  # noqa: PLR0912
46:         super().__init__(with_cursor=with_cursor)

48:         if not display:

50:         elif isinstance(display, str):

53:         self.conn: xcb.Connection | None

57:         xcb_setup = xcb.get_setup(self.conn)
58:         screens = xcb.setup_roots(xcb_setup)
59:         # pref_screen_num is the screen object corresponding to the screen number, e.g., 1 if DISPLAY=":0.1".  It's
60:         # almost always the only screen (screen 0); nobody uses separate screens (in the X sense) anymore.
61:         self.pref_screen = screens[pref_screen_num]

64:         # We don't probe the XFixes presence or version until we need it.
65:         self._xfixes_ready: bool | None = None

67:         # Probe the visuals (and related information), and make sure that our drawable is in an acceptable format.
68:         # These iterations and tests don't involve any traffic with the server; it's all stuff that was included in
69:         # the connection setup.  Effectively all modern setups will be acceptable, but we verify to be sure.
70: 
71:         # Currently, we assume that the drawable we're capturing is the root; when we add single-window capture,
72:         # we'll have to ask the server for its depth and visual.
73:         assert self.root == self.drawable  # noqa: S101
74:         self.drawable_depth = self.pref_screen.root_depth
75:         self.drawable_visual_id = self.pref_screen.root_visual

110:             raise ScreenShotError(msg)

112:             if visual_info.visual_id == self.drawable_visual_id:

118:             msg = "Only TrueColor and DirectColor visuals are supported"
119:             raise ScreenShotError(msg)

122:             or visual_info.green_mask != SUPPORTED_GREEN_MASK

141:         Detects and returns monitor rectangles. The first entry
142:         represents the entire X11 root screen; subsequent entries,
143:         when available, represent individual monitors reported by

145:         """

158:         # XRandR terminology (very abridged, but enough for this code):
159:         # - X screen / framebuffer: the overall drawable area for this root.
160:         # - CRTC: a display controller that scans out a rectangular region of the X screen.  A CRTC with zero
161:         #   outputs is inactive.  A CRTC may drive multiple outputs in clone/mirroring mode.

198:         randr_ext_data = xcb.get_extension_data(self.conn, LIB.randr_id)

203:         return (randr_version_data.major_version, randr_version_data.minor_version)

205:     def _randr_get_primary_output(self, randr_version: tuple[int, int], /) -> xcb.RandrOutput | None:
206:         if self.conn is None:

212:             return primary_output_data.output

51:       block may provide this as an int, string, or both; the string
52:       version is preferred.

55:       are numbered is up to the manufacturer.)

146:     """Dump data to a PNG file.  If `output` is `None`, create no file but return

148: 
149:     :param bytes data: RGBRGB...RGB data.
150:     :param tuple size: The (width, height) pair.
